artifacts.summary: 4-phase plan making assess-repo-health.sh existence-safe with a new phantom_paths diagnostic, re-sequencing /todo's metrics sync after its commit, and adding git-fixture regression cases.

memory_candidates.content: Enumerating candidate files via `git ls-files` reads the git INDEX, not the worktree: a path moved/renamed/deleted on disk but not yet staged is still emitted at its old, now-nonexistent location. Any per-file check that treats 'command failed' as 'file is broken' (bash -n, jq empty, a compiler) will therefore score phantom paths as real defects, and any derived total/status is wrong. Filter for on-disk existence at the single array-population choke point rather than guarding each downstream loop, so counts and future consumers are all fixed from one place. Checks whose failure mode already coalesces to zero (grep -c with a `${c:-0}` default) are incidentally immune and need no guard. Callers that run such a probe before their own commit compound the hazard and should be re-sequenced to measure the tree they actually committed.
